locator.section: 4 / Basic Mechanisms of Ion Fragmentation (Hydrogen rearrangement to a saturated heteroatom with adjacent cleavage)

evidence.curator_note: Section 'Hydrogen rearrangement to a saturated heteroatom with adjacent cleavage', eq 4.37, p.76. The alcohol is n-ionized at oxygen: the odd electron and the charge are localized on O (drawn '+.OH'), so the precursor SMILES carries O+ with one radical electron (convention B). The six-membered transition state brings the delta C-H (map 3, the C2H5-bearing carbon) up to the oxygen radical. ARC COUNT: the book draws 3 arc(s) on the molecular ion and all three fishhooks are printed -- move <1> = the O odd electron (right-hand fishhook next to '+.OH', map 7) into the forming O7-H8 bond; move <2> = one electron of the breaking C3-H8 sigma bond (the large central arc that sweeps from the carbon toward the oxygen) into that same forming O-H bond; move <3> = the other C3-H8 electron (left-hand fishhook) onto carbon map 3, its new radical site. Net: H8 migrates C3 -> O7, giving a distonic ion with a carbon radical (map 3) and a -O+H2 oxonium (map 7), overall still C6H14O+. (mass unchanged). Instantiated for 1-hexanol (M = C6H14O, m/z 102), whose C2H5 terminus appears explicitly in the charge-migration branch (eq 4.38).

locator.section: 4 / Basic Mechanisms of Ion Fragmentation (charge retention, radical-site displacement 'rd')

evidence.curator_note: Charge-retention ('rd') branch of eq 4.37: the carbon radical (map 3) displaces water from the oxonium carbon (map 6) in a homolytic substitution (SHi), closing a cyclobutane ring (map3-map6 bond) and expelling the odd electron plus the charge together as HOH+. (m/z 18, drawn '< 3%'). The book draws the neutral hydrocarbon schematically as 'R--[square]' = R-cyclobutane; instantiated here as R = C2H5 -> ethylcyclobutane (C6H12, neutral, not detected). ARC COUNT: the book draws 2 arc(s) -- move <1> (fishhook off the radical dot on map 3) = the odd electron into the forming C3-C6 ring bond; move <2> (the large arc sweeping toward the O) = one electron of the breaking C6-O7 sigma bond into that same forming C-C bond. Move <3>, the other C6-O7 electron onto oxygen map 7 (the odd electron of the departing HOH+.), is an implicit homolysis hook required for electron balance (not drawn on the page -- the book simply writes HOH+. as a product). 'Charge retention' = the oxygen fragment keeps both the charge and the radical it carried at ionization.

Cross-linked to MOD rules IMS_4_37_rH and IMS_4_37_rd; VERIFIED against their DFS. IMS_4_37_rH '[C]1[C]2[C]3([H]4)[C]5[C]6[C]7[O+.]8[H]9 >> [C]1[C]2[C.]3[C]5[C]6[C]7[O+]8([H]4)[H]9' transfers the H (their H4 = my map 8) from the delta carbon (their C3 = my map 3) to the O radical cation (their O8 = my map 7), moving the odd electron O -> C and turning O+. into an oxonium -- exactly step_rH_hydrogen_rearrangement's bond changes (their chain C1..C7 corresponds to my maps 1,2,3,4,5,6 with O8 = my 7; their skipped index 4 is the H). IMS_4_37_rd '[C]1[C]2[C.]3[C]4[C]5[C]6[O+]7([H]8)[H]9 >> [C]1[C]2[C]3[C]4[C]5[C]6{-}3.[O+.]7([H]8)[H]9' forms the C3-C6 ring bond ('{-}3' on C6), breaks the C6-O7 bond and splits off HOH+. ([O+.]7) while the radical on C3 is quenched -- exactly step_rd_displacement_charge_retention. The cleaved C6-O bond is incident to C6, which is the atom that forms the new C3-C6 bond, so the rule is a correctly encoded radical displacement (no geometry mismatch). Both rule map numberings align 1:1 with this record.
